data.name: Lokraj
data.gender_notes: Lokraj is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name derived from Sanskrit 'Loka' meaning 'people' and 'Raj' meaning 'king' or 'ruler'. It signifies the one who rules over the people. The name Lokraj carries the meaning “Lord of the People” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Lokraj usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the people and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes leadership and governance with compassion and fairness.
data.etymology: Lokraj belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the People.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lokraj total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Lokraj" reflects the rich cultural heritage of ancient India where kings were considered the protector, provider, and ruler of the people. This name evokes a sense of leadership, authority, and responsibility towards one's community or nation.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, this name signifies the one who serves and protects the people with a selfless and compassionate heart, inspired by the divine principles of love, dharma, and duty. The name "Lokraj" embodies the idea of a ruler who governs with the pure intention of serving and uplifting the people, thereby bringing peace, happiness, and joy to the realm.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Lokraj: Ruler of the People. One who governs and upholds the values and harmony of the community, ensuring its prosperity and happiness.

vedic_reference.note: This name is derived from the Sanskrit words ‘राजा’ (rājā) meaning ‘king’ and ‘लोके’ (loke) meaning ‘among the people’.
